text: Leaving the hall. <break time="0.8s" /> I climbed a hill. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked out over a world. <break time="0.8s" /> That had become one great garden. <break time="0.8s" /> Without fences or signs of work. <break time="0.8s" /> There were no small houses anywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> And the men and women. <break time="0.8s" /> Looked and dressed so much alike. <break time="0.8s" /> That I could hardly tell them apart. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting on a seat of yellow metal. <break time="0.8s" /> As the sun went down. <break time="0.8s" /> I thought about why mankind had become so weak and gentle. <break time="0.8s" /> Long ago, I guessed. <break time="0.8s" /> People had conquered nature. <break time="0.8s" /> And made life perfectly safe. <break time="0.8s" /> So there was no more need. <break time="0.8s" /> For strength or courage. <break time="0.8s" /> The struggle having ended. <break time="0.8s" /> Their bodies and minds. <break time="0.8s" /> Had slowly grown soft. <break time="0.8s" /> And this, I thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Was the sunset of mankind. <break time="0.8s" /> The moon was rising. <break time="0.8s" /> When I came down the hill. <break time="0.8s" /> And I looked toward the little lawn. <break time="0.8s" /> Where I had left my machine. <break time="0.8s" /> The lawn was there. <break time="0.8s" /> And the white sphinx. <break time="0.8s" /> Gleamed in the moonlight. <break time="0.8s" /> But the Time Machine was gone. <break time="0.8s" /> I ran wildly. <break time="0.8s" /> Around the sphinx and through the bushes. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was no sign of the machine anywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> And a terrible fear seized me.
